prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology and molecular identity of the incretin hormone GLP-1 that enabled treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: All six opening ballots placed B003 first, but I do not take that as proof of merit; the case rests on the science. The incretin effect, the processing of proglucagon, the identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, its insulinotropic and satiety actions, and its degradation by DPP-4 form a chain of mechanistic physiology that is original, independently replicated and clear. That chain explains why long-acting agonists work and has since produced durable benefit in type 2 diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal outcome trials. Holst established the physiology of GLP-1 secretion and action in humans, Drucker the receptor biology and therapeutic concept, and Mojsov the identification and synthesis of the active peptide. This trio keeps the prize anchored on discovery, which fits the will of Nobel, while the clinical impact is as large as for any candidate on the shortlist.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. Credit for the active GLP-1 peptide is contested, and Habener and others are not among the supplied names, so the list alone cannot settle priority and Mojsov's inclusion may be challenged. Leaving out Knudsen means the prize skips the medicinal chemistry behind liraglutide and semaglutide, which is the step that made the biology a drug. The three-laureate cap forces a choice between physiology and industrial drug design, and any choice will look incomplete. Long-term safety of chronic use of the class is also still accumulating.

responses.point: Svenningsson ranks B003 first but names Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, treating Knudsen as the leading figure behind liraglutide and semaglutide and regarding Mojsov's weight as contested.
responses.response: I agree that Mojsov's credit is contested and I take that seriously. I still prefer her to Knudsen. Mojsov's contribution is to the discovery of the active peptide, which the prize must explain, whereas Knudsen's is chemical optimisation of a mechanism already understood. Where I accept his point is that Knudsen's work was decisive for patients, and if the committee chooses to honour drug development, her inclusion is defensible. I would ask us to settle the Mojsov-versus-Habener priority question from documentary evidence before deciding, not by dropping her for convenience.

responses.point: Perlmann gives B003 the same trio but suggests Knudsen's drug-development work may be better suited to a different recognition, and ranks the unfolded protein response (B043) second.
responses.response: I agree on separating discovery from drug development and I share his judgement that the GLP-1 mechanism is settled. On B043 I partly disagree. I respect Walter and Mori's discovery, and I list it as an alternative, but it has had less impact on human disease so far, and the PERK and ATF6 arms credited to Ron and others sit outside the supplied names. As a second part it would make the credit picture less clean than the CAR-T or cGAS-STING candidates, so I would not rank it above B015 now.

responses.point: Linnarsson ranks the SMN2 antisense candidate (B040) third, calling Krainer and Bennett a clean, complementary pair for a fatal childhood disease.
responses.response: The pairing is clean and the clinical result is real, and my own research field, RNA splicing, makes me more aware of how elegant the mechanism is. That is exactly why I do not let it raise the candidate: the discovery is a rational application of splicing biology, approved only since 2016, with durability still being established and the SMN1 discoverers outside the credited set. I think it is a strong future candidate rather than one for this year, and I would not put it ahead of B015, where the evidence of benefit is broader and longer.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius ranks the imatinib candidate (B010) third and calls it fully mature and arguably overdue, while noting the upstream BCR-ABL discoverers are not credited.
responses.response: I accept that the clinical proof is among the strongest on the list, with two decades of survival data. My hesitation is the one she names herself: the prize story for CML begins with the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL discoverers, who are not credited, so a Druker-Lydon-Sawyers prize would honour development without its discovery foundation. I rank it below CAR-T for that reason, but I would support it if the committee wants a translational second part.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's claim to identification of the active GLP-1 peptide outweighs competing claims by Habener and colleagues cannot be resolved from the supplied text.
Whether the committee prefers to honour GLP-1 physiology only, or physiology plus the drug-design step by Knudsen, is open, and the three-person cap forces the choice.
Whether a two-part configuration, for example B003 with a CAR-T pair, would be better than a single GLP-1 prize is not settled, because only one or two names can be spared from B003.
Maturity of the cGAS-STING candidate (B052) rests on unproven therapeutic impact, and priority among STING discoverers is unclear.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted candidates. I have co-authored work with committee colleague Sten Linnarsson and with Jonas Frisen, but neither is a credited name on any shortlisted ballot, and the profile does not document a tie to any credited candidate; shared Karolinska Institutet affiliation alone is not treated as a conflict.
